text: From a glance, this chart looks standardly bullish, but if you dig deeper, there are some really interesting insights here. April Builder Users: 36,997 HL Users: 235,372 Builder Share: 15.72% May Builder Users: 1,130,357 HL Users: 6,474,080 Builder Share: 17.46% June Builder Users: 2,200,118 HL Users: 7,294,534 Builder Share: 30.16% July Builder Users: 2,229,948 HL Users: 6,122,413 Builder Share: 36.42% Some points: 1. HL Frontend users are decreasing, but builder numbers are staying consistent, which concludes to builders owning a higher % share, but it doesn't necessarily mean that builders are attracting more users from HL frontend users. 2. Builder adoption has basically plateaued. Between June and July, the difference on Builder users was +1.4%. Native HL users was -16.1%. Therefore, builders didn't really gain many new users. Instead, native HL frontend usage actually fell. 3. Given that builder users haven't really changed, this likely means that builders have "stickier" users. Native frontend users declining by more than 1M+ suggests that builder users are more loyal, higher quality, more active traders and/or more integrated into products. Overall, I think just this simple chart could potentially tell the story of Hyperliquid becoming infrastructure rather than a website to trade on.

text: Michael Saylor Opposes Bitcoin Consensus Changes, Advocates for a Simple and Neutral Base Layer Strategy founder Michael Saylor said Bitcoin's biggest threat comes from internal factions rewriting consensus rules and seizing economic rights. He compared Bitcoin's consensus rules to a constitution and opposed proposals including BIP-110, additional covenant machinery, and larger blocks, arguing they could weaken transaction freedom, blockspace scarcity, and network security while increasing validation costs and attack surfaces. Saylor said as the block subsidy halves every 210,000 blocks, miners will rely more on fees to secure Bitcoin, and weakening the fee market could threaten long-term security. He called for keeping Bitcoin's base layer simple, neutral, scarce, and secure, with innovation built at the edges, and protocol changes made only when necessary and conservatively. — link
